headline: Park Entrance Fees and Seasonal Road Closures
reservation: A Custer State Park entrance license is required for all vehicles on SD Highway 87. The highway closes entirely to vehicles in winter, typically from late October until the spring thaw. Campsites and lodges within the park must be booked via the state’s central reservation portal, often months in advance.

days.title: Granite Spires and Narrow Passages

stops.name: Needle's Eye Tunnel
stops.detail: Drive through the 8'4" wide rock opening and view the spire that resembles a needle's eye.

stops.name: Cathedral Spires Trail
stops.detail: Hike among the massive granite fins that pierce the skyline for a close-up look at the geology.

days.driving: Allow 1–2 hours for 14 miles; one-lane tunnels create frequent wait times
days.note: Check vehicle width before attempting tunnels; large campers may not fit.

days.title: High Peaks and Alpine Waters

stops.name: Sylvan Lake Shore Trail
stops.detail: Walk the easy loop around the lake to see the reflections of giant boulders in the water.

stops.name: Black Elk Peak
stops.detail: Trek to the highest point in South Dakota to visit the historic stone fire tower.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; roads are steep with sharp switchbacks
days.note: Black Elk Peak is a 7-mile round trip; allow at least 4 hours for the hike alone.

days.title: Wildlife Loops and Prairie Vistas

stops.name: Mount Coolidge Lookout
stops.detail: Drive to the fire tower for a 360-degree view of the Black Hills and distant Badlands.

stops.name: Wildlife Loop Road
stops.detail: Search for mountain goats on the cliffs and bison in the lower grasslands.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; traffic slows significantly for animal sightings
days.note: Always maintain a safe distance from bison; they are wild and unpredictable.

intel.title: Sylvan Lake Congestion
intel.text: The Sylvan Lake lot often fills by 9 AM during summer weekends. Consider using the shuttle if available or arriving at first light to secure a spot for the Black Elk Peak trailhead.

intel.title: Topographical Interference
intel.text: The deep canyons and granite walls cause frequent GPS and cellular dropouts. Carry a physical Custer State Park map for navigation between the tunnels.

intel.title: Black Hills Supply Towns
intel.text: Gas is available in Custer, Hill City, and Keystone, but not along the Needles Highway itself. Ensure your tank is full before starting the ascent into the spires.

intel.title: Early Bird Advantage
intel.text: Morning light provides the best visibility through the narrow tunnels. Midday often brings motorcycle convoys and heavy tourist traffic that can stall travel.

intel.title: Seasonal Gate Status
intel.text: The highway is strictly seasonal; gates are locked at the first heavy snow. Check the South Dakota DOT website for real-time status of SD-87.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Rapid City or Chadron (CDR); pick up a park pass at any entrance station before heading to Sylvan Lake.
plan.vehicle: Check rental height and width; dually trucks and large RVs are prohibited in many tunnels. High-clearance vehicles are not required but smaller cars handle the tight turns better.
plan.goldenHour: Needle's Eye overlook in the late afternoon for sun hitting the granite textures.
